correctness.rationale: For each primitive binary two-run period, a mixed border fixes the cyclic phase; two consecutive occurrences are one period apart and an interior mixed-border closed occurrence extends. A unary border between consecutive matching runs uniquely gives the bridge intervals, with only t below the full run length remaining maximal. Full runs and the whole word complete the list. Run/bridge counting yields (k-1)(a+b)+3; per-cut bounds yield at most a+b-1 and period-boundary cuts attain it. Two standalone programs verify small instances via different border-counting methods (97 and 48 word cases) and 4,335 larger symbolic instances. Finite testing is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: Two-run binary powers are a natural benchmark for compressed text indexes and maximal closed substring reporting. Exact occurrence endpoints give an all-parameter structural classification; the number of all MCS occurrences is linear in length, and the worst local cut density is governed by the primitive period rather than by repetition length. The sharp cut law addresses a specifically motivated internal-query parameter, not an arbitrary numeric slice or an asymptotic gain.
